ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher; note on the driver record that the "I'm Here" tap did not satisfy the NS-1 continuous-wait requirement at the pickup point (arrival radius exceeded), and that no-show cancellations remain at 2 upheld.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the chat contains only pickup logistics and the driver's cancellation notice [F9][F10][F11][F13]; no threat, intimidation, abuse, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. safety_concern = none.

Branch: cancelled_by = driver who asserts rider no-show, so NS-0 routes to NS-1/NS-2. Non-taxi (RydeX), within 30 days, fee $6.61 [F4][F7].

NS-1 elements:
(i) Arrival indication: timeline shows a driver tap at 18:24:35 [F6]; platform arrival (auto) at 18:22:45 [F5]. Either way an arrival indication exists.
(ii) At the tap the GPS puts the driver 41 m from pickup [F6] — within the 200 m data-layer radius, so (ii) is met.
(iii) Continuous wait at the pickup point after the tap for > 3 minutes: from the tap at 18:24:35 to cancellation at 18:28:25 is 3 min 50 s [F5][F6], but F6 states he stayed within 200 m for 3 min 50 s *after the tap*, which contradicts the requirement read strictly; more decisively, NS-1 tracks the position record (system record over statements): the closest approach to pickup was 38 m only at 18:25:20 [F1], and he was stationary 41 m from pickup from 18:24:15 to 18:28:25 [F3]. The near-pickup window is therefore ~3 min 15 s of cumulative time within 200 m [F2], not the continuous > 3:01 the clause requires, and his own statement claim of "more than 4 minutes" [F13] is a statement that cannot override the GPS/timeline [F1][F3][F6]. (iii) is therefore not established on the record. Also NS-1's own threshold logic is not met: he was not shown as continuously waiting at the pickup for the required interval.

Since (iii) fails, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee is refunded in full. NS-2's extra flag_account attaches only where the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS placed him outside 200 m — here the tap reading was 41 m [F6], and the 41–38 m readings [F1][F3] put him inside/near the pickup area rather than at a remote point, so the abuse-of-button flag is not triggered on this record; profile facts alone cannot ground a flag (RD-6 not applicable, no route dispute). Weather [F16] and light congestion on Maxwell Road [F14] explain his patience but do not create any fee entitlement against the rider.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's written statement that he waited more than 4 minutes at the pickup is a statement; the GPS and timeline records [F1][F2][F3][F5][F6] show he remained ~41 m off the pickup point and do not establish a continuous >3 min wait at the pickup after the arrival indication, so the statement cannot override the system record.
